newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar weakens on steady overnight selling.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar weakens on steady overnight selling.

text.p: FORECAST RANGE 1.3935/1.3975 ASIAN CLOSE 1.3935
RESISTANCE 1.3855 SUPPORT 1.3405 HI 1.3955 LO 1.3930
CANADA OPEN 1.3951/56 HI 1.3955 EUROPE OPEN 1.3938
* The Canadian dollar opened weaker at C$1.3951 (US$0.7167) in
heavy trading on Tuesday after an overnight session marked by
steady selling in Asian and European markets, traders said.
* They said selling in North America could push the Canada
unit to the key C$1.3975 (US$0.7155) level, triggering
stop-loss orders and a move to C$1.4000 (US$0.7142).

The steady weakness in the Canadian dollar could force the Bank of Canada to intervene in support of the currency earlier than expected, said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy.

"The normal intervention level would be somewhere above the C$1.4005 (US$0.7140) area, but there are some rumors in the market that the Bank will come in early at the C$1.3975 (US$0.7155) or C$1.3980 (US$0.7153) level," Farrill said.
Economists said that markets have been driving the Canadian dollar gradually weaker in an attempt to test the Bank of Canada's resolve to hold interest rates steady.
The Bank of Canada last raised interest rates by 25 basis points on June 26 in an effort to bolster the struggling Canadian dollar.
"The markets are basically testing the Bank to see whether its resolve will weaken in holding the line on rates," said Mario Angastiniotis, economist with MMS International.

"The critical area is C$1.3975 (US$0.7155). That's where you unwind completely the monetary conditions tightening that we saw since the last rate hike," Angastiniotis said. "That is key for the Bank because it doesn't want to see easier monetary conditions."
But Angastiniotis said it was more likely that the Bank of Canada would support the currency with intervention before resorting to another interest rate hike.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar dipped to 83.03 Japanese yen from 83.34 on Monday and fell to 1.3332 marks from Monday's 1.3371 marks.
((Paul Simao, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8104))
